class: An agent stops its own stale process by NAME (`taskkill /IM python.exe`, `Stop-Process -Name python`, `pkill python`, `pkill -f <pattern in its own argv>`) instead of by the PID it recorded at start; every matching process on the machine dies - another agent's test run, the owner's live server, or the agent's own shell.
mechanism: The agent did not record the PID of the background process it started, so at clean-up time it could only match by name; nothing refuses a name-based kill.

first_seen.where: user-level standing rule 'Production hosts' R5 (two calling-shell kills that week)
first_seen.evidence: `pkill -f <pattern>` matching its own command line killed the calling shell twice

fix: Stop only PIDs recorded when the process was started; a PreToolUse hook refuses a Bash/PowerShell command that kills by process name or by a pattern, and names the rule (kill by PID).

detection.note: Mechanism due (third occurrence): a project PreToolUse hook on Bash and PowerShell refusing `taskkill ... /IM`, `Stop-Process -Name`, `pkill`, `killall`, `Get-Process <name> | Stop-Process`; fail open on a crash; Tier A check before wiring.

occurrences.where: another project, calling shell killed twice
builder sequence process item (mutation gate fix round 1), ~09:47 IST
occurrences.evidence: `taskkill //F //IM python.exe` killed the owner's live API on :8765 and any other agent's python run; the agent confirmed it; API restarted 09:48, Kite session intact
